thread:
alex: FYI deploybot auto-suggested a rollback after the post-merge canary sweep. metrics look noisy tho, might be a heuristic false positive. asking for quick call on whether we pin or let auto rollback run.

deploybot: [automated] Canary rollout v3.7.2 -> 30% traffic. Signal: error_rate spike above threshold for 3m. Suggested action: AUTO-ROLLBACK -> v3.7.1. See logs: https://ci.redwoodinference/internal/deploy/1745678901

sara: I see the alert, but the spike lines up with a batch of long-tail inference requests from a single customer IP. can we check per-customer telemetry before reverting? :thinking_face:  

mira: quick sanity check: the regression test suite passed on canary earlier, and flame graphs look fine. suspect KV cache eviction noise — we've seen similar transient spikes after cold starts.

anne_ops: If it's a single-customer burst we should be cautious about a full rollback. Proposal: pin v3.7.2 for 15m and run a focused smoke on routing + kvcache warmup, then decide. Who can run pin+smoke? :ear:

alex: I can do the pin and kick off smoke. Command: ```deployctl pin --env canary --version v3.7.2 --ttl 15m``` After pin, I'll run the traffic-replay job: ```infra/replay --from=2024-06-18T12:00Z --filter=customer_id=acct_42 --rate=1rps```

sara: thanks. also add a temporary metric filter to ignore single-customer bursts so the deploybot heuristic doesn't auto-rollback again while we investigate. e.g. set alert scope -> group_by: customer_id, threshold_count: 3

deploybot: [automated] Pin applied by alex: v3.7.2 pinned on canary for 15m. Auto-rollback suspended for pinned resource.

mira: while pin is live i'll run a quick KV warmup script and check p95/p99 latency slices. snippet: ```for shard in $(seq 0 31); do warmup-client --shard $shard --batch 64 & done``` should take ~90s.

alex: Pin done. replay running. initial replay shows error spikes tied to long sequence lengths ~ sometimes >4k tokens; that's outside normal canary distribution. I'm leaning to treat this as false positive; recommend unpin after warmup and let canary absorb with warm cache.

anne_ops: Good notes. Hold until we confirm replay and warmup results. If we still see a multi-customer signal or sustained p95 > 1.2s for 10m, we'll proceed with rollback. Otherwise unpin and monitor. I'll post a short blurb for release notes comms: "Investigated canary alert; transient customer traffic spike caused heuristic trigger; no quality regressions detected; no production rollback executed."

sara: small ask — record the deploybot heuristic parameters that tripped so we can tune: `window=3m, threshold=0.05, group_aggregation=global`. We'll add a follow-up ticket to split threshold by customer.

mira: warmup finished. p95 normalized, replay error_rate back to baseline. Looks like false positive.

alex: unpinning now and letting canary continue roll. deployctl unpin -> ```deployctl unpin --env canary --version v3.7.2```

deploybot: [automated] Unpin applied by alex. Canary rollout continues. No rollback executed.

anne_ops: Closing loop: we avoided an unnecessary rollback. follow-ups: 1) tune deploybot heuristic to group by customer_id, 2) add kvcache warmup step to canary rollout checklist, 3) update runbook with pin TTL guidance. I'll file the follow-up tickets and ping product. :white_check_mark:
